title: RailRoute AI Phase 4 - mixed journey combination engine: delivery report
route_scenario: MYS -> DWR (the product scenario, used for the synthetic test network)
live_api_test_policy: tests/test_live_mixed.py is skipped by default (pytest marker live_api); runs only with RUN_LIVE_API_TESTS=1 and a configured RAILCORE_API_KEY, with a <=6-request budget. The normal suite never touches the real provider.
development_verification: Entirely against httpx.MockTransport with synthetic 997xx trains; the production search flow contains no mock data; the provider integration (phase 1 RailCoreClient/normalizer) is untouched.

architecture_and_algorithm.approach: Additional orchestration layer, not a rewrite: MixedJourneyCombinationService SUBCLASSES the phase 3 TrainChangeConnectionService and inherits its discovery, corridor learning, schedule pool, class filtering, leg generation with transfer-window/horizon/cycle validation, first-leg seeding and budget-aware deduplicated batched availability querying verbatim. The two complete search endpoints are never called and concatenated.
architecture_and_algorithm.new_edge_type: Same-run continuation legs: after alighting at station X on train T (run R), the passenger may keep riding the SAME run R onward from X - a SAME-TRAIN SEAT CHANGE (phase 2 semantics: the passenger stays onboard through the halt while the ticket boundary changes; no transfer buffer or max-wait applies). The run is anchored by the previous leg's actual arrival datetime, so overnight day offsets and per-segment IRCTC boarding dates stay correct and the continuation always belongs to the run being ridden. Boarding a different run of the same train number is excluded.
architecture_and_algorithm.search: Time-dependent earliest-arrival (connection-scan style) chronological expansion over individual ticket segments: a priority queue of arrival events is popped in arrival order; expanding an arrival generates schedule-validated train-change legs (transfer window, running days, day offsets, horizon, no station revisits, consecutive trains differ) plus same-run continuation legs, checks availability through the shared SegmentQueryPlanner, and pushes one new event per confirmed leg.
architecture_and_algorithm.journey_model: A journey is a chronological sequence of individual ticket segments; consecutive segments on the same train run form seat-change groups; transitions to different trains are validated train changes. A single-segment source->destination journey is a direct train: excluded from results, listed in direct_trains without availability claims.
architecture_and_algorithm.limits: No fixed maximum number of seat changes or train changes: depth is bounded only by cycle prevention (no station revisits), the horizon and REPORTED computational budgets. No dominance pruning by design (merging states that share station+arrival-time would discard valid alternative journeys whose earlier segments differ). Duplicate journeys are detected by physical segment signature (train, stop sequences, boarding dates) and recorded once.
architecture_and_algorithm.ranking: CHEAPEST / FASTEST / FEWEST_TRAIN_CHANGES / FEWEST_SEAT_CHANGES with deterministic tie-breaks (fare -> duration -> changes -> seats -> segment count -> journey id). Totals: fare (never estimated; unknown fares leave the total null and are listed per segment), door-to-door duration, transfer waiting time (train-change waits only), segment count, train changes, seat changes, distinct trains.

how_phase_2_and_phase_3_are_reused.phase_3_reuse: Subclassing: _seed_discovery, _seed_pair_pass, _discover_pair, _ensure_station_discovery, _discovery_targets, _fetch_schedules, _learn_schedule, _register_discovered_train, _generate_legs, _push_first_legs, _query_legs and _RunState are inherited UNMODIFIED (the phase 3 engine file was not edited). Only _explore (adds continuation legs + journey signature dedup), assembly, ranking and the response builder are overridden.
how_phase_2_and_phase_3_are_reused.phase_2_reuse: The phase 2 semantics live in the shared components the mixed engine reuses: per-segment IRCTC boarding dates with overnight day offsets (phase 2 _boarding_date semantics, applied to continuation legs), explicit-only availability qualification and the same SegmentQueryPlanner (dedup memo, 25-item batches, budgets enforced before requests, process-wide schedule/discovery caches, per-search availability freshness). Cross-engine consistency is proven by a test running phases 2, 3 and 4 against the SAME mocked network: the mixed engine's same-train-only journeys equal phase 2's combinations and superset phase 3's connections.
how_phase_2_and_phase_3_are_reused.shared_infrastructure: SegmentQueryPlanner (dedup + batching + budgets + caches), InternalAvailabilityStatus normalization, RailCoreClient, budget patterns (MixedJourneyBudgets subclasses TrainChangeBudgets; with_overrides per-request transfer windows) and the ranking conventions. No availability logic is duplicated; no live API call is made by either engine's tests.

files_modified: backend/README.md (Phase 4 section: architecture, algorithm, rules, budgets, ranking, sample, limitations, tests)

phase_2_and_phase_3_untouched.engines_unmodified: same_train_combination_service.py and train_change_connection_service.py were not edited; their endpoints, schemas, semantics and all 126 pre-existing tests pass unchanged.

known_limitations: Same-run continuations only: journeys that alight from train T and later re-board a DIFFERENT run of the same train number are not generated (deliberate, keeps seat changes unambiguous).
No station revisits (inherited from phase 3): journeys riding a circular service a full lap are out of scope.
Discovery is schedule-anchored (inherited): branch stations no fetched schedule reveals need via_stations hints; routes with no through train return an honest NO_CANDIDATE_TRAINS without hints.
Availability freshness is provider-side; per-segment checked_at and oldest last_updated_at are reported but no strict freshness policy is enforced yet.
Seat-change halts are reported per transition (onboard_halt_minutes) but not summed into total waiting time.
Single travel class and quota per search; missing fares leave the total null (never estimated).
Combinatorial growth is bounded by the reported budgets (states, journeys, requests, credits, time, horizon); SEARCH_LIMIT_REACHED says so honestly.
No persistence, no booking, no AI agent (out of scope for this phase).

ready_for_phase_5.notes: All three engines emit self-contained, composable journey objects with explicit journey_type (SAME_TRAIN_SEGMENTS / TRAIN_CHANGE / MIXED), per-segment statuses/fares/boarding dates and explicit segment + transition typing, so the station manager, persistence layer (PostgreSQL/Alembic when genuinely required) and the AI agent can consume them directly. No database was introduced in this phase.
